messages:
anya: quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC — want to nail interface boundaries for validation. thinking: pre-accept (sanity + manifest), accept (bench + perf + kv compatibility), post-accept (observability hooks + canary policy). sync?

leo: +1. can we decide this sprint? we need clear fail vs warn rules. :calendar:

sam: agree. first concrete ask: define the artifact manifest and handshake API between intake and bench. minimal fields only. otherwise bench becomes a fragile mess.

maria: question — how do we handle model variants (float32 vs int8)? single manifest or runtime-specific artifacts?

sam: propose a single artifact_manifest.json with per-artifact entries. sample: 

```json
{
  "model_name": "mistral-7b",
  "model_sha": "a3f9...",
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "path": "mistral-7b-fp32.onnx",
      "dtype": "fp32",
      "opset": 14,
      "quant_profile": null,
      "fingerprint": "sha256:..."
    },
    {
      "path": "mistral-7b-int8.q8",
      "dtype": "int8",
      "opset": 14,
      "quant_profile": "q8_legacy_v2",
      "fingerprint": "sha256:..."
    }
  ],
  "kv_schema": "v1",
  "export_flags": ["no-tracing"]
}
```

sam: fields are strings to keep cross-language parsing easy. runtime teams read per-artifact and pick compatible binary.

eng-bot: pipeline-run 4589 started: ingest -> validate-manifest -> bench-smoke.

leo: tradeoff note: strict manifest validation will reduce runtime surprises but will block a lot of new models early. suggestion: soft-warn for missing optional metadata, hard-fail for incompatible kv_schema or missing fingerprint. :warning:

anya: +1 to that. soft-warn + tag models as "compatibility-risk" visible in registry UI. but hard-fail if kv_schema != current_runtime or if artifact fingerprint is missing. kv cache layout changes cause silent catastrophes.

maria: perf checks — what threshold? p50/p95 regressions? and warm vs cold starts?

sam: minimal proposal: run microbench with canonical prompts. require p50 <= 1.10 * baseline_p50 AND p95 <= 1.25 * baseline_p95 for same deployment config. run both cold-start (empty kv) and warm-start (prefilled kv) profiles. failures block accept.

leo: plus token-level output stability for critical golden prompts — not full determinism but logits drift under X% (we can use cosine on logits). if drift>threshold mark for manual review.

anya: agreed. combine: manifest sanity -> smoke (fingerprint, kv check) -> perf (cold/warm) -> quality (golden prompts) -> metadata gating. soft-warn for missing optional fields. hard-fail for kv/schema/fingerprint/perf-regressions above thresholds.

maria: how do we record decisions? I'll draft a short RFC follow-up PR with checklist and owner assignments.

sam: I'll add the manifest schema to model-registry contract and a small validator lib.

leo: I'll wire the perf harness to run as part of the onboarding pipeline with a lightweight replay of 10 canonical sequences to keep CI time bounded.

anya: owners: maria (validation flow + RFC PR), sam (manifest schema + validator), leo (perf harness + CI integration). i'll own policy decisions for hard vs soft gating.

maria: ok I'll open the PR today and link the checklist.

sam: once PR lands i'll prototype the validator and share a test vector set.

leo: can we add a day-1 fallback plan: if onboarding blocks but model is needed for dedicated customers, platform can route to a pinned variant with a manual exception. ops will track exceptions.

anya: fine, but exceptions require explicit signoff from infra and security. we need audit trail.

eng-bot: pipeline-run 4589: validate-manifest -> WARN missing export_flags for artifact mistral-7b-int8.q8 (soft).

maria: thanks. will include export_flags in PR as optional field and mark its absence as warn.

anya: great sync. will merge checklist after PR reviews. :white_check_mark:
